headline: Chips and Fuel Cells Surge as Thursday's Session Splits Sharply Along Sector Lines
body_html:
Thursday's session ended with a fractured market: advances and declines finished nearly dead even across the 519-name universe — 249 up, 266 down — yet the headline numbers obscured a violent rotation underneath. Semiconductors dominated all comers, posting a sector gain of 8.29%, while Energy added 2.70% and Materials tacked on 1.41%. Everything else finished in the red, with Consumer names off 2.07% and Software surrendering 1.75%, underscoring how narrowly the day's strength was distributed.

The session's standout mover was Bloom Energy, which surged 26.49% on what appeared to be a powerful earnings catalyst, putting the fuel-cell developer atop the leaderboard. Semi-equipment names clustered just behind: FormFactor jumped 26.28% and Ichor Holdings added 20.43%, each amplifying the semiconductor complex's already commanding performance. Memory maker Sandisk climbed 25.99%, reinforcing the narrative that chip-adjacent names were the unambiguous beneficiaries of Thursday's appetite for risk.

The other side of the ledger was equally dramatic. Alnylam plunged 28.31% — the session's steepest single-stock loss — dragging biotech sentiment lower. Fair Isaac slid 17.01% and C.H. Robinson dropped 15.44%, adding financial-data and logistics to a casualty list that stretched across Healthcare, Homebuilders, and Consumer discretionary. In a session where breadth was essentially flat, the day belonged entirely to those willing to concentrate in silicon and electrons.

briefs.headline: Bloom Energy Lights Up the Tape With Earnings-Driven Surge
briefs.body: Bloom Energy finished Thursday as the session's top percentage gainer, rocketing 26.49% in heavy volume. The fuel-cell specialist's move powered the broader Energy sector to a 2.70% advance, one of only four sectors to close in positive territory on the day, and drew fresh attention to the alternative-energy corner of the market.

briefs.headline: Alnylam Suffers Session's Steepest Drop on Clinical Setback
briefs.body: Shares of Alnylam Pharmaceuticals cratered 28.31%, the single worst performance across the entire universe on Thursday. The RNA-interference specialist's collapse weighed on the Healthcare sector, which shed 1.04% on the day, and served as a stark reminder of the binary risk embedded in late-stage biotech development.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Equipment Names Cluster at the Top of the Leaderboard
briefs.body: FormFactor and Ichor Holdings posted gains of 26.28% and 20.43% respectively, joining memory chipmaker Sandisk — up nearly 26% — in a sweep of the session's top-five advancers. The coordinated strength lifted the Semiconductors sector by 8.29%, the widest margin of any group and the clear dominant theme of Thursday's tape.

briefs.headline: US Second-Quarter Growth Restrained by Import Surge, Domestic Demand Holds Firm
briefs.body: Fresh macroeconomic data showed that a rise in imports acted as a drag on overall US economic output in the second quarter, even as underlying domestic demand remained resilient, according to Reuters. Investors parsed the mixed reading against Thursday's sector rotation, with cyclical industrials managing a modest 0.81% gain despite the headline.

briefs.headline: Fair Isaac and Waystar Lead a Rough Day for Data and Healthcare Tech
briefs.body: Fair Isaac tumbled 17.01% while Waystar Holding shed 14.60%, putting financial-data and healthcare software among Thursday's hardest-hit pockets. The losses compounded a broader Software sector decline of 1.75% and suggested earnings or guidance disappointments are prompting investors to rotate away from higher-multiple technology sub-sectors.

briefs.headline: Geopolitical Tensions Simmer as Houthi Attacks Expand and Iran Pressure Mounts
briefs.body: Reuters reported that Yemen's Houthi forces have been launching strikes against Saudi Arabia from Iraqi territory, while separately, the US moved to tighten sanctions on networks supporting Iran's Mahan Air. The developments added a layer of geopolitical uncertainty that likely contributed to Thursday's 2.70% advance in the broader Energy sector.
